also: what’s the dish of the day?

terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for a restaurant’s dish of the day. Ferculum is a dish or course of a meal (Hor. S. 2.6.104; see “course”), and hodiernus “of today” is Cicero’s (hodiernō diē). In a question, the plain adverb is more natural: Quid hodiē coctum est?

phrases.english: What’s the dish of the day?

phrases.latin: Ferculum hodiernum est piscis assus cum holeribus.
phrases.english: The dish of the day is grilled fish with vegetables.
What kind of soup do you have today?

phrases.latin: multaque dē magnā superessent fercula cēnā, quae procul exstrūctīs inerant hesterna canistrīs
phrases.english: and many dishes were left over from a great dinner, yesterday’s, piled up in baskets close by

sources: Lewis & Short: ferculum · Lewis & Short: hodiernus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 68.
